subject: Post-incident - customer-facing RCA summary and action checklist
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@northbridgepayments.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for RCA and timeline after Wed outage

Rafael —

Thanks for the quick incident updates yesterday. Our engineering and risk teams are asking for a short, customer-facing RCA and an itemized timeline we can share with senior leadership and procurement. Specifically:
- Short root cause summary we can paste into our risk notes (2-3 sentences)
- Minute-level timeline (start/end, key actions)
- Concrete mitigations and owners + expected delivery dates
- Any proposed SLA credit or remediation path we should expect

We need something by end of day Friday to include in our internal briefing. Can you confirm?

Thanks —
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Platform Reliability
Northbridge Payments
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@northbridgepayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request for RCA and timeline after Wed outage

Sara —

Appreciate the note and totally understand the need. I've attached a concise customer-facing RCA draft and an incident timeline CSV (attachments: draft_rca.pdf, incident_timeline.csv). Below is the two-paragraph summary and the immediate commitments; we'll follow with a formal package by Friday EOD.

Executive summary (two lines): On Wed 5/29 a serving regression in a newly-rolled batching kernel caused inconsistent KV-cache evictions under high-concurrency traffic, which resulted in elevated token latency and a small subset of sessions experiencing truncated responses. No customer data was exfiltrated and there is no evidence of content integrity loss beyond truncated outputs.

Key immediate mitigations (already applied):
- Rollback of the new batching kernel to stable v3.12 (completed 05/29 15:20 PDT) — OWNER: runtime-team (Dylan)
- Hotfix to KV cache eviction threshold to prevent premature evictions (deployed 05/29 16:05 PDT) — OWNER: infra (Irene)
- Emergency rate-smoothing on the affected routing tier to limit burst amplification (05/29 16:30 PDT) — OWNER: SRE (Marissa)

Planned remediations (deliverables we will provide in formal package):
1) Postmortem narrative + minute-level timeline (this doc) — ETA: 2028-06-01 EOD — OWNER: Rafael
2) Kernel rollout gating: automated canary policy + perf thresholds before any kernel rollout — ETA: 2028-06-10 — OWNER: Runtime (Dylan)
3) KV-cache telemetry and stronger eviction safeguards (telemetry + guardrail alerts) — ETA: 2028-06-07 — OWNER: Infra (Irene)
4) SLA review & proposed credit calculation for impacted customers — ETA: 2028-06-03 — OWNER: Accounts Ops (Marissa)

I'll share the full narrative and attach the mitigation checklist by Friday. Let me know if you want a 30-minute call Thursday to walk leadership through the timeline.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Patel <sara@northbridgepayments.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Northbridge Payments Procurement <procurement@northbridgepayments.com>
Date: Wed, 31 May 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request for RCA and timeline after Wed outage

Rafael —

Thanks, that summary helps. A few follow-ups from risk and procurement:
- Can you confirm whether any tokens were persisted or logged outside our control during the incident window? That's our primary scoping question.
- Procurement wants a clear SLA credit proposal and the raw timeline so finance can model the hit.
- Leadership is asking for a short canary-run plan they can sign off on before you re-enable the new kernel.

We may take you up on the Thursday call. If possible please include a one-page remediation checklist that we can circulate (owners & dates is critical).

—Sara
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@northbridgepayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Northbridge Payments Procurement <procurement@northbridgepayments.com>
Date: Fri, 2 June 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request for RCA and timeline after Wed outage

Sara —

Thank you — short answers up front, followed by attached artifacts.
Q: Any tokens persisted/logged externally?
A: No. We performed an audit of logs and object stores for the incident window (05/29 14:50-05/29 17:00 PDT). No user content or tokens were exported to external storage. Internal debug logs captured truncated payloads but those are ephemeral and stored only in secured, access-controlled logging for 30 days. We will include the log-audit summary in the formal package (attachment: draft_rca.pdf).

Q: SLA credit proposal
A: Our Accounts team will propose a credit consistent with our SLA and the affected throughput for your account. Draft credit proposal will be delivered 2028-06-03 (OWNER: Marissa).

Q: Canary run plan for kernel re-enable
A: Attached is a one-page mitigation_checklist.md with: staged canary (0.5% of traffic for 24 hrs), active perf telemetry thresholds, automated rollback at threshold breach, and a joint signoff step with your on-call. ETA for plan finalization: 2028-06-04. (OWNER: Dylan).

Attachments included: draft_rca.pdf (customer-facing narrative + evidence summary), incident_timeline.csv (minute-level timeline), mitigation_checklist.md (one-page checklist & canary steps).

If you agree, let's schedule a 30-minute review Monday to walk leadership through the canary plan and credit approach.

Best regards,
Rafael
